decisions.claim: B was in a situation where a small boy was rushing out blindly near B
decisions.reason: Turn 1's 'Look out!' directed at B presupposes B is in a situation where the boy rushing out blindly is relevant to B's position.

decisions.claim: B stopped (likely a vehicle) just in time to avoid hitting a small boy who rushed out blindly
decisions.reason: Combining turn 1 (boy rushing out) and turn 3 (B stopped just in time) supports the inference that B stopped to avoid the boy. The parenthetical '(likely a vehicle)' is speculative but the core claim is a reasonable E2 inference.
decisions.counterexample: B could have been on foot or a bicycle, not necessarily a vehicle.

decisions.claim: B was in a position where a small boy could rush out blindly toward them (e.g., on a road or street)
decisions.reason: c4 is essentially equivalent to c2 — both assert B was in a position where the boy's action was relevant. 'Could rush out blindly toward them' and 'was rushing out blindly near B' are the same presupposition from 'Look out!'
